solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: International survey provides precedent

parts.note: an international cricket or rugby match is a Test
to case a place is to survey it before a crime

explanation.surface: A worldwide study turns out to set a precedent for later rulings.
explanation.walkthrough: A TEST match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action whose outcome sets a rule for later similar cases is a precedent-setting one.

clue.text: Decoration shimmeringly glistens at the centre

indicators.note: something shimmering moves and flickers, so the letters are shifted about
only the inner letters of the word are taken, dropping its two ends

explanation.surface: A decoration glints and shimmers in the middle of a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the centre' strips G and S from glistens to leave LISTEN, which 'shimmeringly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering metallic strands hung on Christmas trees are a classic decoration.

clue.text: To speak about money that will get a return makes sound sense

indicators.note: the verb for speaking goes round the other piece

parts.note: to speak is to say

indicators.note: a return here means the money word is turned back to front

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Talking about investments that pay back sounds like good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN is old British slang for money; 'that will get a return' turns it back to front before 'about' wraps the speaking word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanity is soundness of mind, the state of having sound sense or reason.

clue.text: Most of distinct new fashion is uncluttered

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped so most of the word remains

parts.note: distinct means clear
to fashion something is to cut or shape it

explanation.surface: A distinctive new style is described as neat and uncluttered.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean-cut means neat and simple in outline, with nothing untidy or cluttered about it.

clue.text: Mascara conceals blemish

indicators.note: the make-up word holds the answer tucked among its letters

explanation.surface: Make-up is used to cover up a mark on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on skin by a healed wound, a kind of blemish.

clue.text: Some think it's childishly sentimental

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people consider it immature and soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is art or decor of cheap, mawkish taste, so the word serves as an adjective for sentimental.

clue.text: Satirical piece starts to infuriate comedian

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun, as is iron

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch begins to annoy the comic performing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' and 'iron' are both slang for a handgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is saying the opposite of what is meant, a staple tool of satirical writing.

clue.text: Fancy silver raised work embedded in garment

indicators.note: the work piece is set inside the rearranged metal word
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Ornate silver embossing is set into a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads the work upwards. A slipover is a sleeveless pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipover is a sleeveless knitted top pulled on over the head, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Stolen goods are the in thing

definitions.meaning: slang for goods recently stolen and risky to handle
something highly fashionable or exciting right now

explanation.surface: Stolen goods turn out to be what everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang both for stolen loot and for anything trendy or sexy.

clue.text: A new molten outburst could yield hydrogen for example

indicators.note: an outburst is an explosion, so the letters are blown apart and reformed

parts.note: A as written, then N, the standard abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh eruption of molten rock might release hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen is a chemical element that is not a metal, an example of that class.

clue.text: Is vote misrepresented in left-wing council?

indicators.note: something misrepresented is distorted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rigged ballot asks whether a socialist assembly has been misrepresented.
explanation.definitionFit: A soviet was an elected workers' council in revolutionary Russia, a communist body.

clue.text: A class act

parts.note: a, as in 'once a day', means per
a form is a school class

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an outstanding performer; in fact 'A' gives PER and 'class' gives FORM.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to perform, give a performance.

clue.text: Though top's gone missing navigational aid is still going strong

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a sextant is an instrument used for navigation

explanation.surface: The upper part has vanished, yet the old navigation device still works.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving.

clue.text: Alarmingly out of breath Panther pilot finds where to land

indicators.note: alarmingly suggests things thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the breath word is taken out of the big cat's name

parts.note: a pant is a short, gasping breath
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breathless Panther jet pilot is anxiously looking for a landing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes PANT from Panther to leave HER; 'Alarmingly' rearranges HER plus PILOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is an airfield for helicopters, a place for them to touch down.

clue.text: Feeling about for nail dropped in booze

indicators.note: the fastener goes into the drink

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or slang for alcohol
a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles around for a nail that fell into their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Groping is searching blindly with the hands, as in groping for a light switch.

clue.text: Corrupt set going before judge and jury ultimately

indicators.note: the setting word comes first in the build

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
a ref, referee, judges a game

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter only

explanation.surface: A rigged trial is staged in front of the judge and jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt as a verb can mean to rot or decay, which is what putrefy means.

clue.text: Muscle complaint

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brawn or muscular power and a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Fellow unionist's participation in restoration of old tub is uncertain

indicators.note: the two abbreviations take part within the rearranged boat
restoring the old boat means its letters are refashioned

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for Unionist

explanation.surface: A union man helps restore a battered old boat, with an unsure result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration of' rearranges OLD TUB as DOUBTL; 'participation in' puts FU inside, after DOUBT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful means not sure, open to doubt, which is uncertain.

clue.text: A staple cooked with a touch of class is soothing

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters are rearranged
just a touch, the first letter, is used

explanation.surface: A basic foodstuff, prepared with a little style, proves comforting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a touch of' gives C from class, and 'cooked' rearranges it with A STAPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Placating someone means calming or appeasing them, so the verb form fits soothing.

clue.text: Keep up feigned animation after love has flown

indicators.note: feigned means faked, so the remaining letters are disguised in a new order
once the love has flown away it is removed from the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up a show of liveliness once the romance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after love has flown' takes O out of animation; 'feigned' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going or keep it in good order.

clue.text: Having lost stern, sloop drifts into Northern capital

indicators.note: drifting about scatters the remaining letters
having lost signals that a piece is taken away from the boat

parts.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so it is the word's last letter

explanation.surface: A sailing boat with a damaged rear drifts towards a Scandinavian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway, in northern Europe.

clue.text: In hospital duty is rigorous

indicators.note: the duty word sits inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
one's part is one's duty or role

explanation.surface: Work on the wards is demanding and strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan describes a harsh, austere, self-disciplined regime, like ancient Sparta's.

clue.text: I'm delighted with variable energy scheme

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight
Z is a common symbol for a variable in algebra
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled with an alternative energy plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheeze is British slang for a clever plan or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a crafty plan or ruse, a scheme in informal British use.

clue.text: Lava is treated as a kind of liquid

indicators.note: treated means processed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Molten rock is handled as though it were a fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Saliva is the fluid secreted in the mouth, one sort of bodily liquid.

clue.text: French vote in favour — Mitterrand finally unravelled

parts.note: aye is a yes vote

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter

explanation.surface: A French yes vote leaves President Mitterrand's plans finally coming apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Frayed describes cloth or rope whose threads have worn loose, coming apart.

clue.text: Player's initially happy with stroke

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: A tennis player starts out pleased with a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a backhand is a stroke played with the back of the hand facing the ball.

clue.text: Losing heart ruffian turns ugly?

indicators.note: turns means the letters are turned round into a new order
the middle letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A thug who loses courage turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' removes the central F of ruffian; 'turns' rearranges what is left. 'Turns ugly' looks like a phrase but is the indicator plus definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags wit: not fair can mean not good-looking, hence ugly.

clue.text: Nearly all of dough's gone

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, leaving nearly all

parts.note: dough is a paste of flour and water

explanation.surface: Almost all the money has been spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' looks like slang for money, but here it is flour paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Past means over and done with, which is gone.

clue.text: Priest will get round that woman

parts.note: round means plump or fat
that woman is her

explanation.surface: A cleric will win over a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the form of address and title for a Catholic cleric.

clue.text: College in the style of US institute will have final year fiasco

parts.note: à la means in the style of
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: final takes the last letter

explanation.surface: A college modelled on an American institute ends its final year in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster, and a fiasco is a disastrous failure.

clue.text: Belittle exercise in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a lesson is a teaching exercise

explanation.surface: Someone puts others down during a speaking drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to make smaller or diminish, which belittle can also mean.

clue.text: To come to a stop by A-road is normal practice

parts.note: to stand is to stop still
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Pulling up beside a main road is the usual procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-road is a British main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is the accepted norm or usual level, so normal practice.
